title: What is USB Slideshow & Signage for Roku?
content: USB Slideshow & Signage turns a Roku device into a USB-powered slideshow and digital signage player. Add photos, videos, and optional audio files to a USB drive, connect it to a compatible Roku device, and start full-screen playback from your TV.

title: How do I start a slideshow?
content: Connect a USB drive that contains playable photos or videos, open the app, and choose Start Slideshow from the Home Menu. The app scans the USB drive and starts a full-screen slideshow/signage loop when playable media is found.

title: Do I need a phone, computer, or media server?
content: No. The app is USB-first. Place your media on a USB drive and control playback with the Roku remote. A separate phone app, browser upload page, cloud dashboard, or media server is not required for local USB playback.

title: Does the app upload my media to the cloud?
content: No. The app is designed to play media from local USB storage connected to your Roku device. It is not designed to upload your photos, videos, audio files, folders, or media library to a Service Provider cloud storage account.

title: Does local playback work without internet?
content: Local USB playback can work without a Service Provider media server. Internet or network access may still be needed for Roku subscription catalog, purchase, recovery, and entitlement features, as well as Help/FAQ, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, support links, and feedback links.

title: What type of USB drive should I use?
content: Use a USB drive that your Roku device can read. For best results, use a dedicated USB drive for slideshow/signage content, keep files reasonably sized for your Roku device, and use media near the TV resolution shown in Settings.

title: What if the app says no USB is connected?
content: Make sure the USB drive is firmly connected to the Roku device, formatted in a way your Roku device supports, and readable by the Roku platform. If needed, reconnect the drive, restart the app, or try another USB drive.

title: Does every Roku device support USB drives?
content: No. USB support depends on the Roku device or Roku TV model. Some devices may not include a USB port or may have platform limitations around external storage and media playback.

title: Does the app scan folders and subfolders?
content: Yes. Start Slideshow, Gallery, and background music selection can scan folders and subfolders on the connected USB drive so you can organize media in directories and still play it in one slideshow/signage loop.

title: Are hidden or system files shown?
content: The app filters common hidden and system entries, such as dot-prefixed items, lost.dir, System Volume Information, and recycle-bin folders, so they do not clutter the media browser or playback list.

title: What image file types are recognized?
content: The app recognizes common image extensions such as JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, BMP, TIFF, AVIF, HEIF, and HEIC. Recognition is extension-based, and actual display depends on Roku platform support and the file itself.

title: What video file types are recognized?
content: The app recognizes common video extensions such as MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, WMV, WEBM, M4V, 3GP, TS, MTS, M2TS, MPG, MPEG, VOB, and OGV. Actual playback depends on Roku codec, container, device, and file support.

title: What audio file types are recognized?
content: The app recognizes common audio extensions such as MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG, OPUS, FLAC, WAV, MKA, AMR, WMA, and ALAC. Actual playback depends on Roku platform support and the file itself.

title: Why does a recognized file fail to play?
content: The app may recognize a file extension even when Roku cannot play the specific codec, container, file size, damaged file, or media variant. Try converting the file to a Roku-friendly format such as a standard MP4 video or JPG/PNG image.

title: How is slideshow order decided?
content: When shuffle is off, media is sorted predictably by type and title. When Shuffle Slides is on, the visual order for Home Menu Start Slideshow is shuffled before playback begins.

title: How do I turn shuffle on or off?
content: Choose Shuffle Slides from the Home Menu. The menu label shows whether shuffle is currently ON or OFF, and the setting is saved for future app launches.

title: How do I change the slide interval?
content: Choose Slide Interval from the Home Menu and select one of the fixed timing options, such as 3, 5, 7, 10, 12, 15, or 20 seconds. The selected interval is saved and used for image playback.

title: Can the app play videos in the slideshow?
content: Yes. Images and videos can play together in a continuous full-screen loop. Images use the selected slide interval, while videos advance when Roku reports that video playback has finished.

title: What happens if a video cannot play?
content: If a video errors, the app shows an unable-to-play message and skips to the next visual item. If every visual item fails, playback closes instead of looping forever through failed files.

title: Can I use background music?
content: Yes. Choose Background Music from the Home Menu to select an unlocked audio file from the USB drive, or choose OFF to disable background music. Background music is optional.

title: Why does background music stop during videos?
content: Background music is released while videos play so the video's own audio can be heard. When image playback resumes, background music can resume from the remembered position.

title: What if my selected background music file is removed?
content: If the saved background music file is no longer found during a later USB scan, the app clears the stale selection and continues without that background music.

title: What is the Gallery?
content: Gallery is a TV-friendly media browser available from the Home Menu. It shows USB folders and media in a grid, lets you open folders, and can launch playback from selected images or videos.

title: How do I browse folders in Gallery?
content: Open Gallery from the Home Menu, use the Roku remote to move focus, and press OK on a folder to open it. Press Back inside a folder to return to the parent folder, or Back at the USB root to return to the Home Menu.

title: Can I start playback from Gallery?
content: Yes. Select an unlocked image or video in Gallery to start playback from that media context. Gallery playback uses unlocked visual items and available unlocked audio items from the current session.

title: What do locked items mean?
content: Locked items are outside the current free access limit. Locked image thumbnails may be blurred and show a lock overlay. Select a locked item to see the limit message and subscription option.

title: What are the free access limits?
content: Free access may limit larger media collections. Current free-mode limits can include the first 5 folders, first 20 files, first 2 audio files, first 2 video files, and first 5 image files in recursive slideshow/signage mode.

title: What does a subscription unlock?
content: A Roku subscription unlocks fuller access to larger USB media collections and removes free-mode restrictions applied inside the app. Subscription availability, pricing, plans, trials, renewals, and entitlement recovery are handled through Roku.

title: How do I subscribe?
content: Choose Subscribe from the Home Menu or from a limit message. The purchase flow is handled by Roku, and the app uses Roku entitlement information to unlock subscription features.

title: How do I manage my subscription?
content: Subscribed users can open Manage Subscription from the Home Menu when available. You can also manage subscriptions through your Roku account or Roku device subscription settings.

title: What is Fill Screen?
content: Fill Screen scales images to fill the TV display. This can look more immersive, but parts of the image may be cropped if the image aspect ratio does not match the screen.

title: What is Show Full Image?
content: Show Full Image scales images so the complete image remains visible. Borders may appear when the image aspect ratio does not match the TV screen.

title: Can I change the image background color?
content: Yes. Settings include black and white background options. The selected color appears behind images, especially when Show Full Image leaves borders around the image.

title: Where are my settings saved?
content: Settings such as slide interval, shuffle, selected background music, image display mode, and background color are saved in Roku registry storage so they can survive app restarts.

title: What information is shown in Settings?
content: Settings can show display details such as screen resolution and aspect ratio, along with slideshow/signage display controls such as slide duration, image display mode, and background color.

title: Can I use this app for digital signage?
content: Yes. The app is designed for simple USB-based slideshow and signage loops. For best reliability, use a dedicated USB drive, use supported media formats, test your content before public display, and keep backup copies of your files.

title: Can I schedule playlists by time or date?
content: No. The current app focuses on USB media browsing and slideshow/signage playback. It does not provide time/date scheduling, a remote web dashboard, cloud sync, or automatic playlist management.

title: Can the app edit or convert my media files?
content: No. The app plays local USB media when supported by Roku. It is not a media editor, converter, backup tool, or cloud storage service.

title: Why should I compress media near the TV resolution?
content: Large or unusually complex files can be slower to scan, display, or play on some Roku devices. Using compressed media near the TV resolution can improve performance and reliability.

title: What should I do if the USB drive is empty in the app?
content: Check that the drive contains supported photos, videos, or audio files, and that they are not only hidden or system files. If the drive has folders, the app can scan subfolders, but Roku still needs to be able to read the drive and files.

title: Where can I read the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use?
content: Privacy Policy and Terms of Use are available from the Home Menu. These pages may load hosted content, so network access may be required.

title: Where can I get support?
content: Open Support & Feedback from the Home Menu and use the Support Page option shown there. The support resource may open or display an external page or QR code.

title: Where can I send feedback or suggestions?
content: Open Support & Feedback from the Home Menu and use the Feedback Form option shown there. Feedback is optional and is handled by the external form or service used for submission.

title: What information is shown on the About page?
content: The About page shows the USB Slideshow & Signage app identity, app icon, tagline, developer credit, asset credits, and feedback contact information.
